land.text: the Colony and Protectorate of Kenya: 'Modern-day Kenya emerged from a protectorate, established by the British Empire in 1895'; 'In 1920, the East Africa Protectorate was turned into a colony and renamed Kenya'

predecessors.note: Cliopatria relabels British Africa as 'British East Africa' for 1961-1972 and keeps Kenya inside its 2.68 M km2 shape until 1968, which overlaps Kenya's own shape from 1963.

land.text: the Sultan's 'strip along the Kenyan coast', whose sovereignty ceased 'simultaneously with independence for Kenya'

predecessors.note: The Kenya Coastal Strip passed from the Sultan of Zanzibar to Kenya on 12 December 1963 (Sultanate of Zanzibar page).

capitals.name: Nairobi
capitals.note: 'Kenya's capital and largest city is Nairobi.' The page gives no date for the seat, so 'from' is the start year.

keyframe_review.note: 585,506 km2 against the infobox 580,367 km2 total (2.3 percent water): ratio 1.01. Cliopatria's row begins in 1963, the year of independence (12 December 1963), so no earlier keyframe is needed. The shape's northern edge (5.36 N) lies beyond the Natural Earth Kenya outline (4.94 N) and its modern-country join includes South Sudan: it appears to take in the far-north strip Kenya administers (the Ilemi Triangle), which neither the Kenya nor the Shifta War page mentions (unverified: page budget). The Kenya Coastal Strip is inside the shape from 1963; the page reports no other border change, so one shape holds for 1963-2023.
Same outline and area (585,506 km2) as 1963-2023; nothing on the page changes the territory in 2024.

region.text: Kenya: the Colony and Protectorate 'came to an end on 12 December 1963'; infobox 'Dominion: 12 December 1963'

ledger.note: 12 December 1963: Kenya becomes independent of the United Kingdom as a dominion. The page names the country, not a boundary; the Coastal Strip joins on the same day (next event).

region.text: 'a 16-kilometre-wide (10 mi) strip along the Kenyan coast' (the Kenya Coastal Strip); Coast Province is a coarse proxy for it

ledger.note: 12 December 1963: the Sultan's coastal strip becomes part of Kenya. 'the Sultan agreed that simultaneously with independence for Kenya, the Sultan would cease to have sovereignty over the Protectorate of Kenya'; a footnote on the agreement of 8 October 1963: 'the territories composing the Kenya Coastal Strip would become part of Kenya proper'. The Kenya page does not mention the strip; the date is Kenya's independence day, the region is the researcher's reading (a 10-mile strip drawn as Coast Province).

region.text: 'the then Northern Frontier District (NFD) of Kenya', 'the current North Eastern province'

ledger.note: December 1963: the Shifta War over the Northern Frontier District begins. 'The conflict began in the weeks leading up to Kenya's independence' (infobox 'c. November 1963'); 'On 28 December 1963, the Kenyan government declared a state of emergency in the North Eastern Region'. The rebels were ethnic Somali irregulars with 'Somali state support' that became 'vital' from 1963; Somalia is named as counterpart for its claim and support, not as a declared belligerent.
12 December 1964: Kenya becomes a republic. 'On 12 December 1964, Kenya became a republic under the name' Republic of Kenya (infobox 'Republic: 12 December 1964'). Same state and land (rule 2).

region.text: 'the then Northern Frontier District (NFD) of Kenya', 'the current North Eastern province'

ledger.note: October 1967: the Shifta War ends in a stalemate and Kenya keeps the Northern Frontier District. 'The war ended in 1967 when' Somalia's prime minister signed a ceasefire (the page says 23 October 1967 once and 28 October for the Arusha summit); the Kenya page: 'A ceasefire was eventually reached with the signing of the Arusha Memorandum in October 1967', though 'relative insecurity prevailed through 1969'.

wars.name: Shifta War

zones.text: 'the then Northern Frontier District (NFD) of Kenya', 'the current North Eastern province'

wars.outcome: Inconclusive (infobox): 'a stalemate developed'; no territory changed hands and 'the state's territorial status quo would be maintained'. The ceasefire of October 1967 (Arusha Memorandum) suspended the states of emergency and restored diplomatic and economic ties between Kenya and Somalia.
wars.note: Dates differ on the page: 'c. November 1963–1967' in the infobox, the emergency declared 28 December 1963, the ceasefire 23 October 1967 and the Arusha summit on 28 October. The Kenya page adds that the 1962 referendum showed 86 percent of Somalis in Kenya wished to join Somalia and that Britain rejected the result.

certainty.note: Inherited colonial boundaries; the Northern Frontier District frontier with Somalia was contested by arms from 1963 to 1967 and Britain kept the status quo ('no altering Kenya's frontier without the decision of the new Kenyan Government', 22 November 1963). The far-north strip in the Cliopatria shape (Ilemi) is not described on the pages opened and should be soft.

notes: Cliopatria's Kenya shape is the modern country (plus a far-north strip that is probably the Ilemi Triangle) with no change after 1963; the page budget (1-2 pages) was exceeded by one shared page: the Sultanate of Zanzibar page, opened for the Zanzibar dossier, gave the Coastal Strip transfer, a real border move at independence that the Kenya page omits. No ruler strip (no list on the pages). Kenya sent troops into Somalia in 2011 ('In 2011, Kenya began sending troops to Somalia to fight the terror group Al-Shabaab'); the page gives no end and no territory, so it is not a ledger event. Not opened (page budget): the Ilemi Triangle, Migingo Island, the Mazrui 10-mile strip history. Gazetteer name wanted: 'Kenya Coastal Strip' (the 16 km strip along the Kenyan coast that was the Sultan's until 1963). The contest with Somalia names Somalia because it supported the rebels and claimed the district; the Somalia dossier (another part) should mirror the contest. British East Africa overlap: the other row's 1961-68 shape contains Kenya; that dossier should drop Kenya from 1963.
